indicators.title: Grain in commercial storage
indicators.question: Is there more or less grain in Canada's commercial elevators and port terminals than usual for this point in the crop year?
indicators.definition: Commercial stocks of all grains and oilseeds in licensed primary (country) elevators, process elevators and port terminals, from the Canadian Grain Commission's weekly statistics.
indicators.how_calculated: Total stocks at the end of the latest grain week, compared with the same grain week in each of the previous crop years.
indicators.does_not_show: Grain still on farms, which is most of Canada's grain, or food stocks further down the chain. High stocks can mean a comfortable buffer or grain that cannot move; read it with the exports line.

headline.period_label: Crop year 2026-2027, grain week 9 (week ending 4 October 2026)
headline.text: Commercial elevators and port terminals held 7.25 million tonnes of grain in the week ending 4 October 2026. Higher than in any of the previous 5 years for this time of year (2% above the median). Worth a closer look; not by itself a sign of crisis.

indicators.baseline_rule: Same grain week in the previous 5 crop years; at least 3 needed.

indicators.title: Grain moving out through ports
indicators.question: Is grain moving through Canada's export terminals at a normal pace?
indicators.definition: Exports of all grains and oilseeds from licensed port terminals (Vancouver, Prince Rupert, Thunder Bay, the St. Lawrence and others), from the Canadian Grain Commission.
indicators.how_calculated: Sum of the latest four grain weeks, compared with the same four weeks in each of the previous crop years. Four weeks smooth out vessel timing.
indicators.does_not_show: Why the pace changed. Slower exports can reflect rail or port problems, weather, a smaller crop or weaker sales. Direct shipments by rail or container to the United States are not included.

headline.period_label: Crop year 2026-2027, grain week 9 (week ending 4 October 2026)
headline.text: 3.21 million tonnes of grain were exported from port terminals in the 4 weeks to 4 October 2026. Within the range of the previous 5 years for this time of year (4% above the median).

indicators.baseline_rule: Same grain week in the previous 5 crop years; at least 3 needed.

indicators.title: Fresh produce wholesale prices
indicators.question: Are fresh fruit and vegetable prices at the Toronto terminal market unusual for this time of year?
indicators.definition: Daily low and high wholesale prices for 12 exactly defined products (same market, variety, grade, origin and package every day), from AAFC InfoHort.
indicators.how_calculated: For each product, the average of daily midpoints (low+high)/2 in the latest week is compared with the same ISO week in up to 5 earlier years. Earlier years are converted to October 2026 dollars with the all-items CPI (Statistics Canada table 18-10-0004-01). A product is flagged only if this week's price lies outside the full range of those years.
indicators.does_not_show: Retail prices, other cities, or why a price moved. Wholesale quotes for one package type are not what households pay, and a price outside the usual range can reflect quality, supply timing or the exchange rate as well as a shock.

headline.text: Of 12 tracked wholesale prices in Toronto, 2 are higher and 2 lower than in any recent year at this time of year, after adjusting for inflation; 4 are within the usual range, and 4 lack enough history to compare.

indicators.title: Food prices compared with wages
indicators.question: Are grocery prices rising faster than what people earn?
indicators.definition: Year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index for food purchased from stores (Canada, table 18-10-0004-01) compared with the year-over-year change in the average hourly wage rate of employees (Labour Force Survey, table 14-10-0063-01).
indicators.how_calculated: Each series' change from the same month a year earlier, computed here from the published values. The gap is food change minus wage change, in percentage points.
indicators.does_not_show: Who is affected. Averages hide households without wages (pensions, social assistance), regional differences and the many people for whom food takes a larger share of income. Wages here are not seasonally adjusted, so they are compared only with the same month a year earlier.

headline.text: In October 2026, prices of food bought in stores were +2.0% on a year earlier; average hourly wages were +2.2%. Wages have risen faster than store food prices for 2 months in a row.

indicators.title: Food recalls
indicators.question: Are food safety recalls more frequent than usual?
indicators.definition: Recall and safety-alert notices issued by the Canadian Food Inspection Agency, from the Government of Canada Recalls and Safety Alerts open data.
indicators.how_calculated: Count of unique CFIA notices whose 'last updated' date falls in the latest 30 days, compared with the same 30-day window in each of the previous 5 years.
indicators.does_not_show: How much food was affected or whether supply was disrupted. Most recalls are narrow (one brand, one lot). The open data give the date a notice was last updated, not first issued, so counts are approximate.

headline.text: 19 CFIA food recall notices in the 30 days to 18 November 2026. Within the range of the previous 5 years for this time of year (21% below the median).

indicators.baseline_rule: Same 30-day window in the previous 5 years.

indicators.title: Official weather alerts
indicators.question: Which official weather alerts are in effect now, and where?
indicators.definition: Warnings, watches, advisories and statements issued by Environment and Climate Change Canada, from the MSC GeoMet weather-alerts collection. Alerts for the same type, province and issue time are grouped.
indicators.how_calculated: Alerts whose expiry time is still in the future. The page also re-checks GeoMet live in your browser and says which version you are seeing.
indicators.does_not_show: Whether farms, crops or transport are actually affected. Alert areas are forecast regions, not farmland, and we have not yet intersected them with crop maps.

headline.period_label: In effect when checked, 21 November 2026 22:56 UTC
headline.text: 12 official weather alerts in effect when last checked (5 warnings), in 4 provinces or territories.
